description: Authentication (who you are) vs. Authorization (what you can access) vs. Accounting (tracking what you did).
Multi-Factor Authentication - Requiring 2+ distinct evidence types (something you know, have, are, somewhere you are, something you do).
Role-Based Access Control - Granting permissions dynamically based on user job roles rather than individual identity.
Attribute-Based Access Control - Access granted based on attributes (user context, location, time of day, IP address, device security posture).
Discretionary Access Control - Data owner holds full discretion over specifying access rights for other users.
Mandatory Access Control - Strict system-enforced access based on military-style clearance levels and security labels.
Identity and Access Management - Framework of policies and technologies ensuring proper users have appropriate resource access.
Privileged Access Management - Specialized monitoring, vaulting, and auditing dedicated to administrative/root accounts.
Single Sign-On - Authentication scheme enabling access to multiple systems/apps with one set of credentials.
Public Key Infrastructure - Framework managing digital certificates, Certificate Authorities (CAs), and asymmetric key pairs.
Certificate Revocation List - A list of digital certificates revoked by the issuing CA before scheduled expiration.
Online Certificate Status Protocol - Real-time query mechanism used to verify certificate validity without downloading full CRLs.
Advanced Encryption Standard - High-speed symmetric block cipher utilizing key sizes of 128, 192, or 256 bits.
Rivest-Shamir-Adleman - Widely deployed asymmetric encryption/signature algorithm relying on prime factor complexity.
Elliptic Curve Cryptography - Efficient asymmetric cryptography providing high security using small key sizes.
Secure Hash Algorithm - Cryptographic hash function family generating fixed-size one-way digest values (e.g., SHA-256).
Hash-based Message Authentication Code - Combines a cryptographic hash function with a secret key for integrity & authenticity validation.
Transport Layer Security - Modern cryptographic protocol securing internet communications over transport networks.
Internet Protocol Security - Protocol suite securing IP network traffic via mutual authentication and packet encryption (AH & ESP).
Security Information & Event Management - Centralized platform aggregating, analyzing, and correlating log data across an enterprise.
Security Orchestration, Automation, & Response - Platform that aggregates alerts and automates incident response workflows/playbooks.
Endpoint Detection & Response - Software offering continuous monitoring and analysis of host devices to mitigate cyber threats.
Extended Detection & Response - Cross-layered telemetry platform combining endpoints, network, cloud, and email security analytics.
Intrusion Detection System - Passive monitoring technology inspecting traffic to alert administrators of malicious activity.
Intrusion Prevention System - Active inline security appliance detecting AND blocking malicious network traffic in real time.
Data Loss Prevention - Software inspecting content to identify and prevent unauthorized exfiltration of sensitive data.
Web Application Firewall - Layer 7 appliance filtering HTTP/HTTPS traffic to defend web services from attacks (e.g., SQLi, XSS).
Cloud Access Security Broker - Security enforcement gateway sitting between enterprise users and cloud service providers.
Zero Trust Network Access - Security framework granting application access on a strict 'never trust, always verify' basis.
Secure Access Service Edge - Cloud architecture uniting software-defined networking (SD-WAN) with integrated cloud security.
Common Vulnerabilities & Exposures - Public database offering standardized identifiers for known cybersecurity vulnerabilities.
Common Vulnerability Scoring System - Industry standard system assigned to communicate vulnerability severity (0.0 to 10.0 scale).
Common Weakness Enumeration - Standardized category list identifying software and hardware weakness types.
Business Impact Analysis - Systematic process determining operational and financial impacts resulting from system disruptions.
Recovery Time Objective - Targeted maximum acceptable duration a business service can remain offline after a disaster.
Recovery Point Objective - Maximum acceptable age of data lost due to a major disruption, defining backup frequency requirements.
Mean Time to Repair - Average duration required to repair, recover, and restore a failed system component to operation.
Annual Loss Expectancy - Total expected annual financial loss for a specific risk (Calculated: Single Loss Expectancy × Annual Rate of Occurrence).
Single Loss Expectancy - Monetary loss realized each time a specific asset threat event occurs (Calculated: Asset Value × Exposure Factor).
Annual Rate of Occurrence - Estimated frequency or likelihood that a specific threat event will occur within a single year.
